overall: The AG found the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating by email outside a posted meeting, but found no violation in a staff member's email and declined the general allegation; the complaint was resolved by informal action.

allegations.summary: Three June-July emails from a Commissioner to a quorum of the Commission allegedly deliberated on a farmstand wastewater flow matter outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Commission acknowledges that these emails constituted deliberation, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: An August 3 email from the Wastewater Administrator to two Commissioners asking how to proceed on the farmstand proposal allegedly violated the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: The Wastewater Administrator is not a member of the Commission and may convey information and documents to the Commissioners without running afoul of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: General claim that the Commission regularly deliberates and decides matters outside posted meetings, without specific examples beyond the emails.
allegations.key_passage: as complaints must allege violations with a degree of specificity; our office will not conduct broad audits of public bodies based on generalized allegations.

allegations.summary: A June 28 remark by a Commissioner referencing a past matter allegedly suggested recent discussion outside a meeting; the letter notes the 30-day filing rule.
allegations.key_passage: Complaints alleging a violation of the Open Meeting Law must be filed with the public body within 30 days of the alleged violation

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation.
remedy_passage: We order the Commission’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that a similar future violation of the Law may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the Law.
